featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited PVR LIDO Juhu for the first time on 21st Sept 2025 to watch "The God Father" Rerelease!

This property is easy to navigate and it is just right on the main road side.

Really impressed with the colourful entrance. Though it is a smaller in size, but the aesthetical looks stunned me.
It given me dazzling bollywood look and feel!!
The Lobbies from main entrance to each theatres are featuring great interiors 👍👍

This property has 3 screens. While screen 1 and 2 are compact theatres, Screen 3 is a bit bigger.

Seatings are at top most comfort with food tray attached to each seat. Each row has big legroom.

Provided Screen size is maximum with respect to Auditorium size is a big plus.

They equipment Atmos system for even these small auditorium. Only drawback in Audio during my show was there was a beep sound making noise in the background.

Projection clarity is too good.

Airconditioning was just right.

Wash rooms are well installed and maintenaned.

Free drinking water facility is good and appreciable.

F&B items prices are high as usual for a PVR cinema.

Major drawback in this entire premises is Low Mobile Network.

Overall it is a nice and different cinema experience in PVR LIDO. Be prepared to watch movie here in a compact sized Theatres. If you come with an expectation of bigger screen experience, PVR LIDO may disappoint you.
Good idea to bring kids to this theater!!!

Patrons may not realise now, but listening to such high volumes over even a short duration, can and will make one lose their hearing faculty.
This is very serious and ALL CINEMA HALLS SHOULD HAVE A DECIBEL MEASURING SYSTEM IN PLACE.
I KNOW WHAT IT IS TO HAVE A HEARING IMPAIRMENT. My son is hearing impaired.

DO NOT RISK YOUR EARS by allowing cinema halls to force you to listen to such high volumes

featured_reviews.name: Krittika Khandare
featured_reviews.review_text:
I am writing this review to document a serious food safety incident at PVR, Jio World Plaza, BKC.

On 15 January 2026, I attended the 6:00 PM show of Avatar 3 in Audi 6. Before the movie, I purchased food from the PVR counter. While eating it during the show, the final bite contained a visible piece of glass that entered my mouth. I immediately spat it out. The fact that I was not physically injured was purely a matter of luck, this could have caused severe internal injury or worse.

I have video evidence clearly showing the glass shard in the food.

What has been equally disturbing is the way this matter has been handled since. Despite multiple emails, follow-ups, and assurances that the issue was being taken seriously, there were significant delays, inconsistent communication, and ultimately a response stating that no lapse could be established at their end. The only gesture initially offered was complimentary movie tickets, which is entirely inappropriate for a life-threatening food safety incident.

As a paying customer, being exposed to such a risk and then experiencing weeks of delay and deflection has been deeply distressing. This review is being posted so that other patrons are aware and so that this concern is documented publicly after private escalation failed to lead to a responsible resolution.

I hope PVR reviews its food safety accountability and customer handling practices more seriously going forward.

featured_reviews.review_text: This theater has in my opinion, the best IMAX screen in Mumbai. It may not be the biggest, but it’s the newest and most premium. featured_reviews.name: Pooja K
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Jio PVR recently for an evening weekday show. The theatre itself was extremely clean, the seats were very comfortable, and the cooling was VERY strong — honestly, carry a jacket if you’re planning to watch a movie there because it gets quite cold inside. The overall ambience and maintenance were excellent.

Ticket pricing between ₹250–₹500 feels reasonable considering the cleanliness and comfort, especially if booked smartly on weekdays.

But as usual with PVR, the food pricing is absurd. Ordered a ₹350 Schezwan Paneer Wrap and it was a complete waste of money. The taste was terrible and definitely not worth the price. They serve it properly with a tray, plate, and cutlery, but realistically, how convenient is that setup inside a movie theatre while watching a film in the dark?

Popcorn and drinks are also heavily overpriced, and the quantity doesn’t justify the cost either.

Overall: great theatre experience for seating, cleanliness, and ambience — but avoid spending too much on the food unless you’re okay paying premium prices for average quality.

featured_reviews.name: Utkarsha Mhadeshwar
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited PVR Cinemas Phoenix Marketcity Kurla and it turned out to be a fantastic movie experience. It is definitely one of the best places in Mumbai to enjoy a film with friends or family.
The first thing that stands out is the excellent sound quality and screen clarity. The audio system is powerful and immersive, making every scene feel more engaging, especially during action or emotional moments. The picture quality is also very sharp and vibrant, which enhances the overall viewing experience. The theatre is well-maintained, and the seating is comfortable, allowing you to enjoy long movies without any discomfort.
The ambience of the cinema is also very impressive. From the moment you enter, the place feels premium and lively. It is located inside Phoenix Marketcity, so you also get a great mall environment with shopping and entertainment options before or after your movie.
Another major highlight is the variety of food and snacks available. You can choose from popcorn, nachos, burgers, beverages, and more. However, like most multiplexes, the food prices are on the higher side. While the quality is good, you should be prepared to spend a bit extra if you plan to eat there.
In terms of accessibility, the location is very convenient. You can easily reach the cinema by taking an auto rickshaw from Kurla or Vidyavihar railway station, making it a hassle-free destination for moviegoers.
Overall, PVR Cinemas at Phoenix Marketcity Kurla offers a premium and enjoyable movie experience with great sound, visuals, ambience, and accessibility—just keep in mind the slightly expensive food.

featured_reviews.name: Nikhil Aher
featured_reviews.review_text:
🎬 INOX IMAX – R City Mall, Ghatkopar | Honest IMAX Experience Review

I recently watched an IMAX screening at INOX IMAX R City Mall, and here’s a clear, no-nonsense review based on the actual experience.

Overall Experience: ⭐⭐⭐⭐☆ (4/5)

What Works Well:
•	IMAX scale & immersion: The auditorium delivers the signature IMAX feel with a massive screen and powerful surround sound, making it a good choice for big-budget, visually heavy films.
•	Comfortable environment: The hall is clean, well-maintained, and acoustics are solid, especially for action and background scores.
•	Location advantage: Being inside R City Mall makes it convenient with ample food and parking options.

What Could Be Better:
•	Projection quality (3D): While watching Avatar: Fire and Ash in 3D, the visuals felt noticeably blurred. A laser IMAX projection would have significantly improved sharpness, brightness, and depth.
•	Seats: The seating is decent but not premium. For long IMAX movies, better cushioning and ergonomics would enhance comfort.
•	3D clarity: Fast-moving scenes lacked crispness, which slightly broke immersion—something you don’t expect from an IMAX-branded screen.

Final Verdict:
INOX IMAX R City Mall is good for IMAX movies, especially if you value screen size and sound, but it falls short of a true next-gen IMAX experience due to the non-laser projection and average seating. Upgrade to laser projection and better seats, and this could easily become one of Mumbai’s top IMAX destinations.

Recommended for: Big action / spectacle films
Not ideal for: Viewers sensitive to 3D blur or expecting laser-sharp visuals

Beyond its cinematic offerings, Natraj Cinema engages with the community, organizing charity events, fundraisers, and awareness campaigns. The cinema believes in giving back to the society it serves, making a positive impact beyond the realm of entertainment.

In essence, Natraj Cinema is not merely a movie theater; it is a cherished institution that weaves stories, emotions, and togetherness into the fabric of the community. It continues to illuminate the silver screen, bringing joy and entertainment to generations, ensuring that the magic of cinema lives on, one screening at a time.

featured_reviews.name: Venkat Krishnan
featured_reviews.review_text: I saw it from outside and came to know what would be inside. I was a resident of Chembur from 1960 to 1991. I still remember, during the 60s, it was pride of Chembur as it was the only air conditioned  theatre in the area and going there to watch any movie with family and friends was a great pleasure for all. AC was very powerful, seats very comfortable, picture and sound quality excellent, canteen used to serve tasty samosas, snacks and beverages at reasonable prices. Management was talking pains to maintain the ambience and decor. But over the period, due to poor management, improper maintenance, the quality deteriorated gradually and it has come to the present stage. Added to all these, competition from multiplexes has caused further damage. Most surprising is still it continues to run against all odds is something great. I doubt will there be any scope for improvement. The best option will be to sell the land to some potential builder who can build Shopping mall or residential tower, as the place is strategically located (very close to railway station and bus stop ). Rest is left to God.

My visit to INOX Neelyog in Ghatkopar East was a bit of a mixed experience. While the theatre itself is okay, it feels like a bit of a deserted venue. The mall it’s located in is quite old, and despite being owned by PVR-INOX, the place feels stuck in time, lacking the modern amenities you’d expect from their brand. It doesn’t have the same fresh, updated atmosphere as other PVR-INOX theatres.

Its proximity to the Ghatkopar Railway Station makes it a convenient choice for moviegoers relying on public transport.

The seating was decent, but there was nothing exceptional about it. The overall maintenance seemed lacking, and the place just felt a bit neglected. The staff were polite, but the overall service felt a bit lackluster, especially when compared to other PVR-INOX theatres. The staff seemed understaffed, and there were minor delays in service, particularly at the concession stand. As for maintenance, it was evident that the theatre could use some attention. The cleanliness in the common areas and washrooms was below par, and the seats, though functional, showed signs of wear and tear.

The ticket prices were reasonable, but when compared to other PVR-INOX theatres, this one doesn’t justify the price for the experience it offers. Snacks were also the standard fare, but the portions were smaller, and they didn’t feel as fresh.

In summary, while it wasn’t a terrible experience, it felt more like a theatre stuck in the past, lacking the vibrant and well-maintained vibe you’d expect from a PVR-INOX property. It’s good if you're in the area, but I wouldn’t go out of my way for it.

featured_reviews.name: Kartikeya Pathak
featured_reviews.review_text:
PVR Cinema – Oberoi Mall, Mumbai

I recently visited PVR Cinema at Oberoi Mall, Mumbai, and had a fantastic overall experience. Of course, the cinema itself lives up to the PVR standard – clean, comfortable seating, great sound and picture quality, and a well-maintained ambiance. But what really caught me by surprise this time was the food.

We decided to try the hotdogs, and honestly, they were far better than the typical movie-snack expectations. The buns were perfectly steamed – soft, warm, and fresh – which made a big difference in texture. The sausage was juicy and flavorful, and they nailed the condiment-to-meat ratio. Nothing was overly messy or underwhelming – just a really well-balanced, satisfying bite that felt thoughtfully put together rather than rushed.

Another nice touch was the small Costa Coffee counter inside the cinema area. It’s not a full café, but they do serve the essentials. We ordered an iced latte, and it was surprisingly good – strong but not bitter, with just the right amount of milk and ice. It was a refreshing complement to the hot food and added to the overall premium feel of the experience.

All in all, PVR Oberoi Mall offers more than just movies – it’s clearly putting effort into creating a quality experience across the board, including the food and beverage options. Whether you’re here for a blockbuster or just want a relaxed evening out, this location delivers on multiple fronts. Definitely looking forward to going back.

Visited MovieTime Cinemas at Hub Mall with a group of friends on a Friday, expecting a good movie experience, but it turned out to be quite disappointing.

The experience started on a positive note. The security staff were welcoming, the common area was clean, and there were plenty of food options available. However, the popcorn wasn’t worth the price.

The washrooms were also decently maintained. The real disappointment began when we entered the auditorium. There was a strong foul smell throughout the hall, making it very uncomfortable to sit. The seats were old, broken, and clearly not maintained for a long time. What surprised us even more was that the auditorium wasn’t cleaned after the previous show empty popcorn tubs, Coke cups, and other litter were still lying around. There were even mosquitoes and flies inside the hall, which completely ruined the overall experience.

The only reason I’m not giving a one-star rating is because the screen quality and sound system were actually quite good.

For a theatre in a mall, basic hygiene and maintenance should never be compromised. I sincerely hope the management focuses on cleaning the auditoriums and renovating the seating, as the current condition is far below expectations.

Cleanliness: 1/5
Seat Comfort: 1/5
Screen Quality: 3/5
Sound Quality: 3/5
Food & Beverages: 2/5
Staff: 4/5
Value for Money: 2/5

Overall Rating: ⭐⭐

featured_reviews.review_text:
Movie Max Goregaon - Honest Review

Visited Movie Max Goregaon with friends to watch Pushpa 2, but the experience was disappointing for several reasons:

1. Parking Charges: The two-wheeler parking fee is ₹50, which is very high for a single-screen theater. Even premium theaters like PVR or INOX charge less.

2. Toilet Facilities: The number of toilets was very limited, leading to long queues. The toilets were also very small, which was inconvenient for the crowd.

3. Drinking Water: There was no drinking water facility available, which was surprising and inconvenient for the audience.

4. Sound Quality: The sound system was not loud enough, and I missed many dialogues during the movie. This was a major letdown.

Overall, the theater didn’t meet basic expectations for comfort or amenities. I might not visit again unless these issues are addressed. Would recommend exploring better theaters in the area for a more enjoyable movie experience.

I had a very good experience at PVR ICON Infiniti Andheri (W) Mumbai in Mumbai. It is one of the best places to watch movies with friends and family. The screen quality is excellent, and the sound system is powerful, which makes every movie more enjoyable. Many auditoriums here use advanced sound like Dolby Atmos for an immersive experience.  
Infiniti Mall
The staff is polite and helpful, and the entry process is smooth. Online ticket booking is easy, and the theatre usually manages crowds well, even on weekends. The washrooms and waiting area are also neat and hygienic. Snacks like popcorn, cold drinks, and fast food are available inside. The prices are a bit high, but the quality and overall experience are worth it.
The location inside Infiniti Mall is also very convenient, as people can enjoy shopping and food before or after the movie. It is easy to reach by public transport and private vehicle. The atmosphere is safe, friendly, and perfect for entertainment.
Overall, PVR Andheri offers a great movie experience with good comfort, sound, and screen quality. I would definitely recommend it to anyone looking for a premium cinema experience in Mumbai.

I had read quite a few negative reviews about this place, but ended up booking a ticket anyway because I didn’t have many other options. To my surprise, the experience turned out to be genuinely pleasant.

The hall is small, but it’s clean and well maintained. Unlike most modern theatres where you enter from the front, this one has an entrance from the back, something that instantly gave me a nostalgic, old-school cinema vibe. The screen may be on the smaller side, but both the picture and sound quality were impressive.

The biggest highlight, though, was the ticket price. At just ₹90 for a 4 PM show, it’s hard to beat the value.

If you miss the charm of how movie halls used to be in the ’90s, this place is definitely worth a visit.
